questions.q: What is an accounting event in Oracle Fusion Subledger Accounting?
options: Any change at all made to any record in a subledger
A business occurrence inside a subledger application that may require a journal entry
A scheduled nightly batch job with no business meaning
A report that lists all transactions for a period
questions.explain: Only occurrences with potential financial accounting impact, like validating an invoice, qualify as accounting events.

questions.q: What is the relationship between an event class and an event type?
options: They are two names for the exact same thing
Event type is a broader category and event class is the specific occurrence within it
Event class is a category of transaction (like Invoices), and event type describes the specific thing that happened within it (like Invoice Validated)
Event classes only exist in Receivables, not in Payables
questions.explain: Event class groups a category of business transaction; event type narrows it down to the specific occurrence.

questions.q: A supplier invoice is validated, and later its amount is adjusted. How does SLA see these two occurrences?
options: As identical events with no distinction possible
As the same event class (Invoices) but different event types (Invoice Validated vs. Invoice Adjusted)
As two completely unrelated event classes
SLA cannot see adjustments at all
questions.explain: Both occurrences belong to the Invoices event class, but each has a distinct event type that lets rules treat them differently if needed.

questions.q: Why does Oracle classify events into event classes and event types instead of leaving rules to detect transaction type themselves?
options: To slow down the accounting process intentionally
To give consultants a stable, documented vocabulary to attach rules to, instead of writing custom detection logic in every rule
Classification is purely cosmetic and has no effect on rule-writing
Because the General Ledger requires it directly
questions.explain: The classification lets a consultant pick an event class and event type from a list when building rules, rather than hand-coding detection logic.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of something that would NOT be an accounting event?
options: Validating an AP invoice
Applying a customer receipt in Receivables
Editing a supplier's mailing address with no financial impact
Adding a new fixed asset
questions.explain: Only occurrences with potential financial accounting impact are accounting events; a non-financial edit like an address change is not.
